newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 8.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 8. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The official National Commission of Human Rights said riots in the West Java town of Tasikmalaya as well as in Sanggau Ledo in West Kalimantan were engineered by third parties. It said its members found leaflets in Tasikmalaya which incited people to take to the streets in protest, while those in Sanggau Ledo rioted because of a land dispute.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said 1997 would be a tough year for Indonesian diplomacy as Nobel laureate Jose Ramos Horta would continue to raise the East Timor issue, adding that "Indonesia-bashing" had become a popular sport among non-governmental groups.

Armed Forces chief General Feisal Tanjung pledged to arrest the "masterminds" behind riots in East and West Java last year. He said the authorities had identified the culprits but still needed more proof to arrest them.

Indonesia's embassy in the Netherlands said that local news reports which said an Indonesian colonel had been arrested by Dutch police for trying to smuggle out about 20,000 ecstasy pills had been manipulated. The mission said the news was designed to tarnish Indonesia's image.
Six people died, including three in the provincial capital Kupang, when cyclone Phil hit East Nusa Tenggara province late last month.
